name: BotBuster
description: Protects configurable paths from bots using a lightweight JavaScript browser verification challenge.
project_description: BotBuster guards a configurable set of URL paths against automated / DDoS-style traffic with a lightweight JavaScript browser-verification challenge, with no CAPTCHA and no third-party service. It runs as a high-priority Symfony HTTP middleware (DdosProtectionMiddleware, priority 300, responder) that intercepts requests before Drupal routing. For each request whose path (or path+query) matches an admin-configured wildcard pattern, the middleware checks for a valid browser token in a cookie (default cookie name botbuster_token). If the token is missing or invalid it returns an HTTP 503 challenge page; a small script (js/challenge.js) stores the server-issued token in a cookie and redirects the visitor back to the original URL. The token is an HMAC-SHA256 value signed with the site hash salt and carries an expiry, so it cannot be forged offline and expires after a configurable lifetime (1 hour to 7 days). Protected paths, token lifetime, cookie name, enable/disable and all challenge-page text are managed at /admin/config/system/botbuster (route botbuster.settings, permission 'administer site configuration'). On config save and on cache flush a ChallengeFileGenerator service writes two files under private://botbuster/ : challenge.html (the rendered challenge template) and botbuster.json (the runtime config the middleware reads without a full Drupal bootstrap). The module refuses to operate without a configured private file system ($settings['file_private_path']), enforced via hook_requirements. It provides no entities, no plugins, no Drush commands and no permissions of its own; its only permission dependency is core's 'administer site configuration' on the settings form.
